targets.review_note: Two letters on consecutive folded levels align only when their original indices have opposite parity: the fold lies halfway between their indices and must be between letters. Conversely, any increasing sequence of equal letters with alternating index parity is realizable by placing folds at consecutive pairwise midpoints; these fold positions are increasing and each segment contains its selected letter, so the pile starts at the bottom and has no gaps. A two-state longest-subsequence DP per letter therefore computes the exact optimum.

targets.review_note: For a fixed maximum distance, unwrap each bride position into three neighboring copies of the circle. A feasible bottleneck matching can be uncrossed to preserve circular sorted order, so it is a cyclic shift: sorted groom i matches extended bride index i+s for one common integer shift s. The allowable bride interval for groom i is exactly [a_i-bound,a_i+bound], yielding an allowable integer interval for s. Intersect those intervals using monotone pointers, and binary search the minimum bound. Repeated positions remain separate participants; the answer is at most floor(L/2).
